# Severed Lands history — private campaign chronology

1. Before the wound: the Severed Lands already exists. Natural arrivals and lifetime returns occur independently of Warden technology. All transported people share the origin described in DM-SECRETS.md; locally born descendants do not.
2. Warden engineering: seven primary Anchor stations and subsidiary regulators support stable conditions and controlled individual early return. The Wardens attempt permanent mass passage and tear the boundary. The connected wound becomes known as the Rift.
3. Closed Vigil: custodians suspend elective passage and redirect the system to containment. The shutdown outlives its designers. Natural crossings continue; maintenance deteriorates and stations fail. Dead arches are later gathered at the Door Graveyard.
4. Settlement: Thornwall, Nexus and the other communities grow around viable ground. Returners organize around the hope of voluntary early departure, while Stayers invest in local futures. Exact dates of the ancient events remain uncertain, not their demonstrated causal order.
5. Hearth Row, years before this campaign: V authorizes an inadequately understood bypass. A street is displaced and people die or become trapped. V conceals their responsibility and much of what they know, then concentrates on cautious containment work.
6. Immediately before arrival: Hadran sells the mill conductors through Fen. Edda sponsors the Glasshouse test with one of them. Damage propagates across a network already close to failure.
7. The campaign: mill pulses, Glasshouse/Waystation failures and the Cairnfields atlas lead to Hearth Row and the observatory evidence. Illegal Nexus bypass work draws the tears into a common pulse. This physical synchronization is the Awakening.
8. The finale is unresolved until played. The party can restore regulated return and containment, maintain containment alone, or cause/suffer an actual failure. A personal return never erases what happened here.
